why: Muster names its own panes, and the daemon knows each pane by that name: it goes into the request that makes the pane. A pane is named so that it can be told which pane it is: its process is born knowing the name as MUSTER_PANE. These cases pin the spelling a mint produces at an instant and a seed, since a name is a contract with whatever has read one. The properties no single spelling can state - that a drawn name is never handed out twice, and that later names sort after earlier ones - are asserted natively in the driver.

cases.name: a pane's name spells the instant it was made and its entropy
cases.why: The shape every pane's name has: `p`, five characters counting ten-second ticks since 2026, and four drawn from entropy. Pinned, because a name that changed shape between versions would strand every pane already carrying one in its environment.

cases.name: a name says when its pane was made
cases.why: The front of a name counts ten-second ticks since 2026, which is what stops two Musters that never speak to each other minting one name unless they mint within ten seconds of each other - and what makes names sort into the order their panes were made. The same entropy as the case above, one tick later: only the front moves.

cases.name: panes made in the same ten seconds are told apart by the end of their names
cases.why: The last four characters are the only thing keeping two panes apart when the tick they were made in cannot, which is the case every split a script makes falls into. A running Muster draws them from the machine's entropy; a case draws them from a seed, so the name it expects can be written down here.
